overview: This 668-page file documents Japanese politics under the U.S. occupation, chiefly from 1948 to early 1949. It combines diplomatic reporting on cabinet crises, elections, labor disputes, political purges, and occupation policy with Hatoyama Ichirō’s extensive purge appeal and a historical study of Japan’s socialist, communist, and labor movements.
interest: Hatoyama’s diaries and appeal show how he defended his wartime record; the restricted study supplies detailed party histories, biographies, and election data.
